claims.text: Approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling induces sufficient lattice strain and grain refinement in CoCrFeNiTi to lower the activation barrier for metastable FCC solid-solution formation.
CoCrFeNiTi has a VEC of approximately 8.0-8.5, which favors FCC stability.
Atomic-radius mismatch contributes to the FCC/BCC phase stability of CoCrFeNiTi.
SPS at 1000°C exploits the milling-induced defect density to produce greater than 99% theoretical density.
SPS at 1000°C remains below the threshold for excessive Ti-driven HCP precipitation and grain coarsening.
Six hours is an inflection point at which lattice strain is maximized without excessive oxygen or carbide contamination.
Long milling durations in refractory high-entropy alloys can introduce carbide or oxide contamination.
Six-hour milling produces a high dislocation density and a nanocrystalline grain size below 100 nm.
The milling-generated nanostructure suppresses HCP formation through kinetic trapping.
A short SPS dwell at 1000°C permits diffusion and densification without significant grain growth or decomposition into HCP or Ti-rich phases.
FCC phase stability in CoCrFeNiTi is governed by VEC greater than 8.0 and low atomic-radius mismatch.
Stored strain energy from six-hour milling overcomes the kinetic barrier to FCC formation.
The 1200-1400°C range is associated with Laves-phase or TiO precipitation in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed processing route will produce a single-phase or FCC-dominant CoCrFeNiTi solid solution.
The processed alloy will have greater than 99% relative density, greater than 400 HV hardness, less than 2 vol% HCP, and less than 0.5 wt% oxygen.
The predicted hardness arises from grain-boundary strengthening and solid-solution hardening.
As-cast CoCrFeNiTi typically has hardness below 200 HV, significant porosity, and Ti-rich segregation or HCP precipitates.
Sintering above 1100°C or milling beyond 10 hours causes excessive HCP precipitation or grain growth, reducing hardness and increasing brittleness.
Milling for less than 4 hours produces insufficient lattice strain, leaving a lower-hardness multiphase material.
Low-load Vickers testing at 100 gf can isolate grain-boundary strengthening from precipitation hardening.

contradictions.description: The intervention prescribes exactly 6 hours of milling, while the uncertainty field states that the transition threshold may vary by ±1 hour.

The precipitation/decomposition threshold is described inconsistently: 1000°C is said to be below a 1200-1400°C precipitation range, but the boundary predicts excessive HCP precipitation or grain growth as soon as temperature exceeds 1100°C.
The predicted targets are >99% density and <2 vol% HCP, but falsification requires <95% density or >10% HCP, leaving broad outcomes that fail the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
